name: Vibration Frequency Estimator
blurb: rough first natural frequency from geometry and material
intro: The first natural frequency of a beam (cantilever, simply supported, fixed or free) or a simply supported plate such as a PCB, from its size and material, with an optional point or component mass. Closed-form Euler-Bernoulli and thin-plate formulas (Blevins, Leissa); good for a first check before FEA.

inputs.label: Length / span
inputs.help: Free length of a cantilever, span between supports, or the plate's long side.

inputs.label: Added mass
inputs.help: At the tip (cantilever) or centre (beams); spread over a plate (components).

examples.title: 100 × 80 × 1.6 mm PCB with 40 g of parts, 60 Hz fan

usage: Give shape (cantilever, ss, fixed, free or plate), for beams the section (rect, round, tube), material (or custom with E in GPa, rho in kg/m³, nu), length/span, width and thickness in mm (or outer/inner diameter in mm), an added mass in g (tip/centre point mass for beams, smeared over a plate) and optionally the excitation frequency in Hz. It returns the first natural frequency in Hz, the first modes, the part's mass, the equivalent static sag, a chart of f1 against length and a warning when f1 is not at least 2x the excitation. Use it to check that a bracket, arm, rod or PCB will not resonate.
sources: R. D. Blevins, 'Formulas for Natural Frequency and Mode Shape', table 8-1 (beam eigenvalues)
A. W. Leissa, 'Vibration of Plates', NASA SP-160, simply supported rectangular plate
D. S. Steinberg, 'Vibration Analysis for Electronic Equipment' (PCB as a plate, octave rule)
Rayleigh's energy method for a beam with a point mass
